# Atlas: The Cala Knight - Canon Card

<!-- generated from content/studio/canon/glossary.json by scripts/canon_card.mjs; do not edit -->

## Premise

**The gods tried to save tomorrow. The Architect stole it.**

> Long ago, the world began running out of tomorrows.
> Six gods tried to save it, each in their own way. But their miracles clashed, and the world began to break. A mortal known as the Architect built the Great Kilns, sealing the gods away and restoring the passage of time.
> Centuries passed. Brass clocks measured the hours, porcelain held them, and lanterns lit the kingdoms. People lived, laughed, and forgot how close the world had come to ending.
> Now the porcelain is cracking. Forgotten memories are awakening, and entire villages are losing hours.
> You are an independent traveller. Your first duty is simple: mend what is broken.

## Naming rule

- Title stays Atlas: The Cala Knight. Every new proper name is an Elvish root (Tolkien's Quenya or Sindarin) plus a plain English word, or plain evocative English.
- Build names from roots, never from existing Tolkien names (no Gondor, Elrond, Silmaril, Voronwë, Tamar).
- At most two names per first letter across races, gods and the Architect. No near-twins such as Nira/Nara.
- Names must be easy to say in Thai and English. Avoid th and heavy consonant clusters.
- Every key English word (Hearth, Oath, Watch, ...) is used in at most one key name.

## Titles

- **Cala Knight**: Q cala, light. A rare legendary title held by a handful of historical heroes, numbered by person. NOT the player order; players never earn it.
- **Kilnwatch Wardens**: Plain English. Optional player faction at Kilnwatch Bastion, joinable at Lv 10.
- **Cala Keep**: Q cala + Keep. Kept as the historical Cala Knights' keep; unassigned in play until a story needs it.
- **The Last Cala Knight**: the most recent person to hold the title, a woman. No ordinal is ever stated; how many Cala Knights there were is unknown. Her name, race, era and the thing she left unfinished are revealed only through traces (Ch 0-VIII). Expansion I retraces her story.

## Race culture (older drafts, proposed)

- **Maro Folk**: Hearthfolk (old working name, now Maro Folk): ordinary people who preserve home and community. Old small-story moment: an elderly lantern-maker keeps a lamp lit for a customer who promised to return thirty years ago (loss theme: forgetting ordinary days).
- **Ondo Forge**: Stonekin (old working name, now Ondo Forge): builders, smiths and kiln engineers. Old small-story moment: a smith polishes a tiny hammer every morning because their apprentice died before completing it (loss theme: work left unfinished). Ch I race focus in the locked card: Ondo Forge + Daro Guard.
- **Linde Folk**: Elenborn (old working name, now Linde Folk): long-lived artisans of star-patterned porcelain. Old small-story moment: an elf visits a bench where a human friend once sat; the tree beside it has grown around the seat (loss theme: outliving shared memories). Locked-card Ch II focus: Tava Kin + Linde Folk (later moved: Linde resolves in Ch IV). Appearance: long-lived (earlier name Lunar, elf-like).
- **Daro Guard**: Oathguard (old working name, now Daro Guard): watch-keepers bound by inherited duty; identity is endurance, vigilance and inherited duty, not aggression. Old small-story moment: a young watch-keeper rings a bell each evening though nobody remembers what the warning meant (loss theme: duty inherited without explanation).
- **Tava Kin**: Wildkin (old working name, now Tava Kin; earlier Beastfolk/Furral): animal-featured people who celebrate fleeting life. Old small-story moment: a baker keeps making an awful cake because it was their grandmother's favourite and everyone pretends to enjoy it (loss theme: joy that cannot be repeated). Festival town famous for painted pottery and terrible traditional cakes. Appearance: animal-featured people (earlier name Beastfolk/Furral).
- **Silme Seers**: Lomewalkers / Ummari (old working names, now Silme Seers; earlier Dark-Lunar): seal-listeners who perceive echoes in porcelain and interpret vibrations and memories trapped in fired porcelain. Old small-story moment: a child hears humming through a porcelain wall and learns the melody belongs to a mother they may never meet (loss theme: remembering what never happened).

## World rules

- **world_structure** (chosen): Hybrid World: shared persistent world, open regions, shared hubs, travel network, instanced dungeons/boss encounters; not everything instanced; regions can be managed/loaded separately.
- **settlement_model** (chosen): Three community tiers: Ancestral Homelands (six), Mixed Settlements (trade towns at crossroads, rivers, ports), Shared Regional Hub (Kilnwatch Bastion).
- **centres** (proposed): Polycentric world: Kilnwatch Bastion is the adventurers' centre but does not monopolise economy or governance; routes form a network, not all via Kilnwatch.
- **landmass** (chosen): One main continent with three terrain groups, no hard borders, with transition zones (foothill forest, plain beside cliffs, rivers from mountains to plain). Green Lowlands (Maro Bell, Linde Glaze), Stone Highlands (Ondo Kiln, Daro Post), Old Wilds (Tava Fair, Silme Echo). Six towns must NOT be laid in a ring around Kilnwatch.
- **world_scale** (chosen): Balanced World / Balanced Exploration: distances give a sense of adventure with villages and points of interest between towns; fast travel unlocked by progress; no kilometre figures until tested on a playable map. Design targets (first walk, no fast travel): town to nearby monster area 2-4 min; to key exploration point 4-8; to field boss 5-10; to neighbouring town 8-15; across several regions 15-30 min; Region 1-4 km2.
- **travel_tiers** (chosen): Three travel layers: local (walking/mount), regional (main roads, mountain passes, transport), convenience (fast travel to discovered points/hubs, with limits). No fast travel to everywhere at game start. Regional shortcuts unlock via exploration/progress.
- **route_types** (proposed): Three route personalities: Main Roads (safe, settlements, convoys), Wilderness Trails (shortcuts via forest/foothills, monsters/resources), Ancient Routes (old roads and ruins, secrets). Example: Maro Bell -> Ondo Kiln either main road via a trading community or shorter foothill trail.
- **streaming** (chosen): Hybrid Seamless Regions: continuous travel inside large regions, transition points between some regions, dungeons as instances; region gateways are natural features (long bridge, pass, tunnel); map structure World > Region > Zone > Point of Interest; Playable / Reserved / Future area states.
- **great_kiln_effect** (proposed): Great Kilns shape terrain: some valleys have time anomalies; old ruins near trade routes; some areas change with chapter events; some old routes abandoned due to Kiln effects; special areas scattered, not every region magical; revealed gradually.
- **homeland_vs_chapter** (proposed): A race's homeland is not always the area of the chapter tied to that race (Linde, Daro, Silme homelands need geography of their own; do not force homelands into Nara Reach/Vinya Hollow/Silme Deep).
- **production_order** (chosen): Initial production: Prologue + Ch 0-II: six homelands at starter scale, Kilnwatch Bastion, main adventure areas of Maro Valley, Ondo Heights, Tava Grove; Ch III-VIII open new regions and expand old ones. Reserved areas protect routes needed later.
- **chapter_region_order** (chosen): World map order of chapters/regions: Ch 0 Maro Valley > I Ondo Heights (Luma's Still Kiln) > II Tava Grove (Rena's Remembrance Kiln) > III Nara Reach (Nara's Ember Kiln) > IV Vinya Hollow (Vinya's Green Kiln) > V Silme Deep (Olo's Glass Kiln) > VI Tira Ridge (Tira's Sentinel Kiln) > VII Kilnwatch Bastion > VIII The First Kiln. Story order need not equal geographic order; do not lay chapters in a line on the map.
- **boss_placement** (proposed): Chapter boss site types: Bellkeeper bell/lantern site; Brass Castellan old fort/industrial structure; Jubilant Collector anomalous festival area; Tithe Warden debt/collection place; Unwilting nature outside its cycle; Unborn Witness ancient ruin/memory vault; Sworn Sentinel pass or oath site; Counterfeit Hour inside or beneath the Bastion; First Regulator inner First Kiln. Field/Dungeon/World boss each placed by site logic, not one per zone.
- **weather_season** (proposed): Only hints: Ch VIII visible wound - districts experience different seasons simultaneously and roads lead to places that no longer exist; Ch I - streets freeze for minutes; no stated climate, weather or season cycle for any town.
- **volunteers_road** (chosen): Volunteers' Road: route of the first volunteers through the chapter regions; each region has a bell, marker or memorial (not identical in every region). Examples: Maro Valley bell that rings too early; Ondo Heights hammer missing its brass fitting; Vinya Hollow empty stone seat with yearly flowers.
- **mixed_settlement_example** (proposed): Example journey: Ondo Kiln (smith sells gear) -> mixed settlement on the road (Tava merchants, Silme explorers, mixed-level adventurers) -> Kilnwatch Bastion (trade, news, events). Not a mandatory quest route.
- **mixed_race_towns** (proposed): Race home towns are not the only place each race lives: towns hold a majority local race plus craftspeople, traders and travellers from other races; no fixed ratios (Ancestral Homelands / Mixed Settlements / Shared Regional Hub model).
- **race_not_destiny** (proposed): Player race does not decide destiny or profession: race gives a cultural starting perspective and a suggested hook only; players may pick a different motive; Ondo/Silme players are not forced into smithing/runes.
- **cross_town_ties** (proposed): Proposed cross-town relationships: Bram-Torren old friends; Pip-Isil pen-pals; Elin-Nelli exchange flowers/sweets yearly; Garran-Vessa shared a watch night with mismatched memories; Sarn-Lasse both keep records and find contradictions.
- **hooks_converge** (chosen): All six races' hooks converge on the same lean-year injustice via the brass-edged short-stamped birth token (millions have one, no power, no lifespan prediction, never required or checked; optional dialogue may acknowledge it generically).
- **scale_conflict** (proposed): Open conflict: the chosen walk-time targets (town to neighbouring town 8-15 min, across several regions 15-30 min on first walk) do not match the repo's 400x400 world with hour-scale travel (1 unit = 1 m). Not reconciled; the design targets and the repo scale need an owner decision.
- **structure_layers** (proposed): Layers: (1) physical geography = the new 11-district geography, authoritative for places, routes and distances; (2) playable maps = existing content (maps, hunting areas, dungeons, monsters, portals); (3) progression (levels, XP, farming, parties); (4) narrative (prologues, chapters, events); (5) world services (economy, travel, bind points, streaming). Progression and narrative run over the same maps with independent rules. Five principles: geography never changes to solve a level problem; town access is not wilderness safety; every town has a primary economic or social identity; a chapter opens a story, not necessarily a road; one world graph governs portals, boats, roads and fast travel.
- **danger_model** (chosen): Fixed monster levels with real danger; no world-wide level scaling. Fixed-level wilderness bands with a small overlap between neighbouring zones.
- **convergence_travel** (chosen): After each race prologue (Lv 10) the first trip to Kilnwatch is a one-way guided caravan; walking stays possible; later trips use the ordinary travel network.
- **first_content_target** (chosen): First content target is Lv 1-15, chapter 0 (Maro Bell + Kilnwatch), then expand.
- **walk_minutes_meaning** (proposed): District-link walk_minutes are relative distance, not literal minutes, until one playable route is measured on a real map.
- **enforced_rules** (proposed): Three rules enforced as data validation: (1) geographic graph integrity: every cross-district portal is a district link, a declared transport link or a listed legacy portal (GEO-09); (2) progression reachability: each race reaches Kilnwatch from Lv 1 to 10 by a protected route or unlocked transport, and the Ch 0-II critical path has valid encounters (not yet automated); (3) one authoritative content registry: stable IDs, no duplicate IDs, no retired names (existing gates). GEO-10 requires link priority and encounter bands on every district.

## Landmarks

- **The Great Bell** (ระฆังใหญ่): It hangs between two towering cliffs among hundreds of brass lanterns; giant porcelain ribs protrude from the valley walls; a winding lantern-lit road leads tiny travellers to the bell. Composition: hanging lanterns (foreground) -> village road (path) -> Great Bell (landmark) -> porcelain ribs (mega-forms)

## Kilnwatch Wardens

Joining quest: q-warden-join-01 "A Place on the Watch" (Lv 10): repair a damaged signal-post lantern, deliver the incident report, sign the Wardens' public service ledger. No exam, no prophecy, no birth check.

| Rank | Thai | Requirement | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runner | รันเนอร์ | joining quest | Warden board quests, +10 storage slots, faction affiliation title |
| Warden | วอร์เดน | 100 Warden reputation | +20 storage total, Warden cloak cosmetic, 5% discount on Warden consumables |
| Elder Warden | เอลเดอร์ วอร์เดน | 350 Warden reputation | +30 storage total, lantern accessory cosmetic, convenience teleport to Kilnwatch Bastion |

Never gated: main story and chapters, dungeons, raids, world bosses, markets, ordinary storage, equipment progression, every Cala Knight discovery, no faction-exclusive combat power

Leave / return: resign at the registrar any time; rank and reputation are kept, bonuses pause and resume on rejoining; no fee.

Legend link: the Wardens keep an incomplete ledger associated with the Last Cala Knight; membership gives no claim to her title.
